title: Access strata and permission synthesis: RBAC v2 topology and mapping
creator: Priya Singh
description: Design a cohesive RBAC v2 role model that maps resource hierarchy to scoped access strata, defines permission synthesis rules, and integrates with SSO/SAML claims, audit logging context, and admin controls. Deliverables: canonical permission matrix, role-binding precedence algorithm, migration strategy for existing roles, audit tagging conventions, and feature flags for controlled rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical permission matrix covering top-level resources (Org, Project, DedicatedPool, Instance, Route) with read/write/admin/operational actions and deny semantics
Algorithm for role-binding precedence and conflict resolution documented and prototyped
SAML group-to-role mapping spec with claim normalization and fallback rules
Audit log schema extension with role_binding_id, elevation_reason, and request_scope tags
Migration plan that preserves existing tenant-level behavior and provides rollback path
End-to-end tests for binding precedence, temporal elevation, and audit tagging passing in CI
decisions: Adopt a strata model: map resources to access 'strata' (Org, Region, Pool, Instance, Route) instead of flat scopes to enable tenancy and lateral admin controls
Default policy: deny-by-default with explicit allow rules; introduce explicit 'implicit-admin' scope only for super-admin bindings
Role bindings are first-class objects with unique role_binding_id used in audit logs to trace attribution
Temporal elevation (breakglass) implemented as a time-bound role_binding with justification stored in encrypted audit field
SAML mapping: prefer explicit role claim mapping if present; otherwise apply group-name normalization and prefix matching to find candidate roles
tradeoffs: Strata model increases conceptual overhead for integrators compared to simple scope strings but enables clearer admin isolation and routing policies
Recording role_binding_id in every audit event increases log size but provides deterministic forensics for incident investigations
Migration with alias bindings is more complex but avoids large-scale customer friction; requires background reconciliation job
Implementing deny rules early complicates policy evaluation but avoids privilege creep long-term
high_level_design_notes: Resource graph: resources are nodes with typed relationship edges (contains, peers-with, managed-by). Each node maps to a strata label used for permission checks.
Permission synthesis: permissions are boolean codes computed from ordered binding evaluation: explicit-deny -> direct-allow -> inherited-allow -> role-defaults. Short-circuit at explicit-deny.
Bindings: role_bindings point to principal (user/service-account/SAML-identity), role (set of permissions), resource_selector (strata-aware), optional time_window, and metadata (reason, ticket_link).
Precedence: direct bindings on resource > bindings on parent resource > global bindings, with an explicit overrideable affinity tag for platform operators
SSO/SAML: map incoming assertion groups to internal principals and role_bindings at sign-in; for unattended flows map service account claims using trust anchors
Audit: extend existing event contract with new fields: role_binding_id, effective_permissions_snapshot, evaluation_path, elevation_request_id (if temporal).
migration_steps: 1) Inventory current role bindings and infer strata mapping using heuristics (orgId -> Org, poolId -> Pool)
2) Create alias role_bindings pointing to inferred strata with 'migration:inferred' tag and disabled=true
3) Run reconciliation job for 2 weeks to surface gaps (metrics: unmatched requests, denied-but-previously-allowed)
4) Notify tenants with migration report and opt-in window to confirm bindings
5) Flip alias bindings to active during a controlled maintenance window; keep rollback flag for 48 hours
6) Remove legacy binding semantics after 90 days of no incidents; archive mapping for audit
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flag gating for strata evaluation and audit enrichment (internal-only)
Phase 1: enable read-only migration aliases for 10 pilot customers
Phase 2: enable write path with temporal elevation and SAML mapping for pilot customers
Phase 3: broader opt-in for all self-serve orgs; monitor deny-rate and support queues
Phase 4: full default-on for new orgs and deprecated legacy branch after 90 days
test_plan: Unit: policy evaluator permutations including explicit-deny, parent inheritance, and affinity overrides
Integration: SAML sign-in mapping with group claim variations (prefixed, nested groups, missing claims)
E2E: simulate breakglass elevation, verify audit fields and timeline, ensure automatic revoke
Load: eval path instrumentation to ensure latency impact < 5ms p95 on auth-critical path
Security: run threat-modeling checklist and red-team for privilege escalation vectors
open_questions: How do we represent cross-region admin roles that must not imply data-plane access in other regions? (affinity tags vs explicit deny)
What's the maximum allowed retention for encrypted elevation justification to satisfy legal teams?
Do we allow wildcard resource_selectors for plugin integrations or require explicit globs?
Operationally: how will support escalate when a binding_id resolves to a deleted role?
notes_for_reviewers: Review the precedence algorithm for edge cases where multiple parent chains exist (shared pools)
Validate SAML mapping examples with Identity team for Okta/Azure AD common claim shapes
Check audit schema extension against storage and retention cost estimates
Confirm migration cadence is acceptable to Customer Success (avoid billing-impacting windows)
